title: The three jewels, now
hook: the Buddha, the dhamma, the sangha, as you know them after five years
tomorrow: why did the Buddha hold up a handful of leaves?

segments.voice: Yesterday, your verses: same words, a different reader. The verses stayed. Today, a week of looking back comes round, and the three jewels with it.

Every shop has a first customer, and almost nobody remembers who it was. The Buddhist story remembers its first two by name. Tapussa and Bhallika, merchants traveling a trade road, came upon the Buddha soon after his awakening and offered him food. Then they asked to become his followers. And here's the odd part. They took refuge in two jewels, the Buddha and his teaching. Not three. There was no sangha yet. No community to go to. Just two men on a road, and a teacher who had nobody yet.
screen: `TWO MERCHANTS ON A ROAD.` → `REFUGE IN TWO JEWELS.` → `NO SANGHA YET.`

segments.voice: The sangha came after: the first monks, then more, and in the Vinaya a father searching for his missing son becomes the first lay follower to go for refuge to all three. Three jewels: the Buddha, the dhamma, the sangha. Three places to rest. A refuge is a shelter you go to in a storm, not a fortress you never leave. You go in, and you come back out a little steadier. Now hold up this week, one day at a time. The Kalamas, told to know for themselves: his own words. Assaji, the beginner with one verse: the great story. The arahant and the bodhisattva: many doors. Thus have I heard: the sources. One arrow, not two: the first words. Two kitchens, two verses: the verses stayed. Look again and the jewels are in all of it. The Buddha, as someone who showed a way and handed back the test. The dhamma, as words you've heard, carried and tried. The sangha, as the beginners, elders, grandparents and friends who passed it to you. Five years on, the three may not look the way they did on the first day. They're still three places to rest.
screen: `THE SANGHA CAME AFTER.` · `A WEEK, ONE DAY AT A TIME.` · `THE JEWELS IN ALL OF IT.` · `THREE, FIVE YEARS ON.` · then, large: `THREE PLACES TO REST.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes. On three breaths, rest in each in turn: the Buddha, the dhamma, the sangha. If you go for refuge, you can say the old Pali silently, Buddham saranam gacchami, I go for refuge to the Buddha, and on through the three. Then let the rest of the sit be just that, a place to rest.
The three jewels: the Buddha, the dhamma and the sangha, the three refuges. The first followers had two; you have all three.
Your line: three places to rest, wherever you are. A week of looking back, done.

howItsDone: Buddhists go for refuge to the Buddha, the dhamma and the sangha, often by reciting the three refuges, three times over, at the start of a service, a retreat or a daily sit.

fork.setup: a friend moving across the country says, 'my practice is tied to my temple. once i leave, it's gone.' what do the three jewels say?
options: the jewels go with you: the Buddha's example, the dhamma you carry, and friends to find there.
she's right; refuge only works inside the building where you first took it.

chat.meaning: The first followers took refuge on a trade road, before a sangha even existed. The three jewels travel; they are places to rest, not a building.

tie.story: Tapussa and Bhallika took refuge on the road, in two jewels, before the sangha existed.
tie.friend: Mai can carry the Buddha and the dhamma to college, and look for the sangha there.
tie.you: where do you rest when you're far from home?

Tapussa.meaning: one of two merchants, the first lay followers

Bhallika.meaning: Tapussa's companion, the other first lay follower

sangha.meaning: the community on the path; one of the three refuges

Buddham saranam gacchami.meaning: I go for refuge to the Buddha

sources.ref: Vinaya, Mahavagga 1.4 (Tapussa and Bhallika take refuge in two jewels)

notes: Mahavagga 1.4 paraphrased: the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika offer rice cake and honey and become the first lay disciples, taking refuge in the Buddha and the Dhamma (dvevacika). Mahavagga 1.7: Yasa's father, searching for his son, becomes the first lay follower to take refuge in all three. Confirm.

Practice offers the traditional Pali refuge line (Buddham saranam gacchami) for those who go for refuge; nothing new is composed. The recitation 'three times' (dutiyampi, tatiyampi) is standard. Confirm.

Day 1767 ('Refuge, again') covered taking refuge again; this day's new angle is the two-jewel refuge of the first followers and the week's review. Confirm no repetition of 1767's hook if it has since been written.
Shape: review (games.recall holds the six carries of days 1779-1784; the day's word, the three jewels, is still taught lightly). Mai's storyline: college in the fall, far from her chùa and ông.
Surprising fact: the first lay followers took refuge in only two jewels, because the sangha didn't exist yet.
